title: Dance halls, advertising trucks, tailgate bucking, and Chris Kelly's blues
summary: Jobs for bands like Rene's, Sunday tailgate competitions between bands, and why Chris Kelly was the greatest blues trumpeter.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: jobs would a band like Rene play? Well he played advertisements, Sunday dances for clubs at home, and then he played clubs. Halls like the Corporators, Economy Hall, the Poitier Hall, the Jean-Amé Hall, the Fethian Tempher, all those old dance halls at that time. They had clubs mostly give dances, and you found men sponsored dances of their own and they charge admission. But they all had advertisements. The dances mostly was on Sunday night and Monday nights for colored people. And they would advertise and you would catch five and six bands on Sunday on trucks, what they called tailgate music. And they would meet at various corners and what we call jam and nah, they would call it bucking. And they would back the tailgates together, that's where they'd get the tailgate music from and they would buck. One would play a number and then the other one would play another number back and the people would clap to find out what band was the best. A band like Rene, and Buddy Pity, some other parts of the city, it might be Kitori and maybe Louis the Main band and was different ones, Chris Kelly and maybe Sam Morgan band. On Sundays that, because they all would advertise, it would advertise where the dance would be so that night you would know and what band you'd pick out that play the music that suits you, that you would go to the dance. But Chris Kelly and Buddy Pity was two of the greatest trumpet players on the greatest. And Chris was the greatest. He still, I've heard nobody yet play the blues like Chris Kelly, blues like Kelly's Love. If you've seen Corrine, please tell her to come home. And a lot of old blues that he played. He could get something out of the way nobody else could. He was really great. And I don't think anybody have a record that Chris Kelly made. And he was the greatest blues player I ever heard. And I've played with many trumpet players who could play the blues, but he was one of the best. To my idea. He was really great.
